EXPORTED AUDIT HEAD


ASSURANCE BOUNDARIES
A useful reference.
A bounded claim.
Demonstrated locally
  • Explicit agent, tool, resource and environment grants.
  • Classification ceilings and exact-host egress checks.
  • Intent- and policy-bound, expiring approvals with separation of duties.
  • Transactional cost reservation and refusal of duplicate execution.
  • Emergency stop before reservation, plus tamper checks on audit records.
Required before production
  • Authenticated identities and trusted resource labels.
  • A connector that cannot bypass the gate.
  • Independent key custody and externally anchored audit checkpoints.
  • Timeouts, idempotency, cost metering and recovery for external side effects.
  • Reviewed deployment architecture, threat model and residual risk acceptance.
The reference cannot stop an already-running callback, authenticate an approver on its own, inspect network traffic, detect prompt injection semantically, or make an external action atomic with SQLite. The budget is a database-lifetime cap on declared reserved costs—not a billing system.
